transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12 09:23 PT
Duration: ~48 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (CTO - Argent ML), Diego Alvarez (ML Eng), Priya Reddy (Infra), Sam (PM)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on integration surface area — how Argent ML would plug Redwood into their existing LangChain/LlamaIndex pipelines, whether to route through their gateway/proxy or call Redwood directly, expectations around rate limits and tenant quotas, and what observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, streaming webhooks) are available for production.

Topics: SDKs (Python/TS), LangChain & LlamaIndex connectors, gateway vs direct API, auth (mTLS/API key/SSO), per-route rate limits and quotas, observability hooks (logs/traces/metrics), streaming & function calls, Dedicated vs Hosted for compliance.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and then we want to hear how you plan to integrate Redwood, especially around LangChain and your gateway setup.
[00:18] Laura (Argent): yeah, thanks, Maya. So high level we're replacing our current hosted calls to—um—several providers with one platform, and want predictable latency. Diego will talk through the ML flow.
[00:30] Diego: sure. We run a LangChain orchestrator in GKE, mostly Python. Calls go through our internal API gateway (kong) where we add auth headers and per-customer routing. We also have a LlamaIndex-based retrieval layer.
[00:47] Ravi (Redwood): cool, couple questions: are you using LangChain's REST runtime or the new retriever APIs? And is LlamaIndex embedded locally or in a managed vector DB?
[00:55] Diego: LangChain agents + retriever, and vectors live in Milvus. LlamaIndex is used for some pre-processing; sometimes we call models via a central gateway to enforce quota.
[01:10] Priya (Argent Infra): our infra constraint — traffic must go through our gateway for auditing and header enrichment. We prefer the gateway to act as a proxy rather than embedding third-party SDK keys on every host.
[01:25] Maya: understood. Redwood supports both direct API calls and a gateway/proxy model. You can either let each service talk to Redwood SDK directly with rotated API keys, or use a central sidecar that forwards requests and injects headers. We also have a gateway integration guide — I'll share.
[01:40] Sam: is there a recommended pattern with LangChain? We use LangChain wrappers in prod.
[01:48] Ravi: yes, we have official examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. For LangChain we provide a client that implements the llm API used by the chain — in Python it's a drop-in: from redwood import RedwoodLLM, etc. With LlamaIndex, we show how to wrap the Redwood embeddings and streaming generation. Maya will send the links.
[02:10] Laura: what about rate limits and quotas — we need per-tenant quotas and hard throttles at the gateway.
[02:18] Maya: Redwood supports per-api-key rate limits and usage quotas. For Dedicated customers we can map API keys to tenant IDs and enforce per-tenant monthly token quotas and per-second concurrency limits. For Hosted there are rate-limit headers you can read and we can set per-key caps.
[02:36] Priya: important — we need a 429 response at the gateway level and a graceful fallback path (cached answers) for our user-facing UI. Can Redwood send back a structured error that our gateway can translate?
[02:48] Ravi: yes, we return a JSON error with an error.code field like LIMIT_EXCEEDED and headers like x-redwood-remaining-tokens and x-redwood-rate-limit-reset. Some transcription note: sometimes header names are slightly different per env but that's the idea.
[03:05] Diego: streaming — we rely on token streaming for partial responses in the UI. Do you support SSE/websocket and how does that work through a proxy?
[03:14] Maya: Redwood supports server-sent events and chunked streaming. If you have a proxy you can either pass through the stream (recommended) or terminate and re-stream; passing through preserves latency. We can provide examples for kong/NGINX to properly proxy chunked responses and keepalive.
[03:33] Priya: auth concerns — can we do mTLS from gateway to Redwood so keys don't leave our network? We also need SSO for console access.
[03:41] Ravi: mTLS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted supports API key and SSO for console with SAML/OIDC. For Private we can put the control plane in your VPC and configure HSM/KMS for key management.
[04:00] Sam: observability — what tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns do we get?
[04:07] Maya: console provides per-request token counts, cost breakdown, and per-route latency histograms. We expose hooks: you can send a request_id header and we return trace ids; we also have a tracing integration that exports spans to your Jaeger/OTEL collector. There are webhooks for request-complete events including token counts.
[04:28] Diego: nice, we want to correlate user_id -> request -> token spend. Also want to see top prompt templates that cause cost spikes.
[04:36] Ravi: our Cost API can tag requests with metadata (customer_id, feature_flag) using x-redwood-metadata. The dashboard can filter by tags and we can emit alerts when a prompt set exceeds a threshold.
[04:50] Laura: security review — SOC 2 and network isolation. We'll need the security pack.
[04:55] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 and the VPC onboarding checklist. For Dedicated we can sign an NDA and provide more detailed architecture docs.
[05:05] Diego: on the SDK side, latency — are there client-side best practices for async batching to reduce token cost but not add latency?
[05:15] Ravi: there's a few: use the client-side batcher we provide for Python/TS which accumulates micro-batches and respects per-request latency SLOs, enable prefix caching where possible, and prefer streaming for interactive UIs. We'll share config knobs: max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, and per-route priorities.
[05:35] Priya: any compatibility issues with current LangChain version? We run LangChain 0.1x (local trunk).
[05:42] Ravi: we maintain examples for the main LangChain stable and nightly; there can be small API surface changes, but our adapter sits at the LLM interface so it should be minimal. If you need, we can open PRs to your internal libs or provide a patch.
[05:58] Laura: we do want a gating proxy that can do header enrichment, tokenization metrics, and small prompt rewriting for safety. Does Redwood support prompt pre-processing hooks?
[06:08] Maya: Redwood has a pre-request hook in the Dedicated/private control plane where you can run a lambda to modify payloads (safety transforms), or you can do that in your gateway. For Hosted we can provide a policy layer (prompt filters) as an add-on.
[06:24] Diego: edge case: our orchestrator sometimes replays KV cache tokens — how do you manage KV cache when using multiple short-lived containers?
[06:33] Ravi: we offer a managed KV cache layer for Dedicated which persists cached keys across instances, and policies for cold-start warming. For Hosted we have prefix caching suggestions; if you use our SDK, KV cache is managed locally with an optional central store.
[06:49] Sam: cost model question — if we run heavy embedding workloads plus generation, any recommended separation of routes or models to control spend?
[06:57] Maya: yes, route separation is recommended. Use cheaper embedding models or offload to Quantized endpoints for embeddings, and route high-priority generations to a smaller dedicated pool. We can annotate routes so billing is split by model + route tag.
[07:15] Priya: regulatory — do you support data residency in EU?
[07:20] Maya: Hosted has EU regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions and Private can be fully on-prem.
[07:28] Laura: what about latency SLOs? Our SLAs require p95 under 350ms for short prompts.
[07:34] Ravi: Dedicated can be tuned with GPU pools and autoscale policies to meet p95 targets; we'll run a short benchmark with your prompt set to validate.
[07:46] Diego: integration wiring question — for LangChain we currently call openai.ChatCompletion. We want a drop-in adapter so we don't change chain code.
[07:55] Ravi: we provide that — the adapter exposes the same method signatures as OpenAI client; you can set REDWOOD_API_KEY and point LLMPChain to the Redwood adapter and it's transparent. Example snippet we'll send.
[08:10] Laura: if we go gateway-first, how do we handle API key rotation? We don't want to roll keys across all pods.
[08:18] Maya: use a single gateway identity with a long-lived key and enable short-lived signed tokens for backend services using our token service. For Dedicated/Private, you can use mTLS and Vault integration.
[08:33] Priya: logs — do you provide raw request/response payloads in logs for debugging?
[08:40] Ravi: we can provide auditing logs that include request metadata and token counts; full payloads are optional and can be turned on in Dedicated/Private for debugging under a restricted retention policy. Hosted scrubs PII by default.
[08:55] Diego: got it. A few blockers for us: proxy config examples, LangChain adapter code, and rate-limit header names.
[09:03] Maya: noted — we'll send those as part of the follow-up.
[09:10] Sam: timeline question — we want a PoC in the next month. If we do Dedicated trial, how long to provision?
[09:17] Maya: Dedicated trial typically 5-7 business days to provision a small pool; Private takes longer (2-4 weeks) depending on network and compliance. Hosted is immediate.
[09:28] Laura: ok, good. Can you also give a checklist for support during POC — who owns what?
[09:33] Maya: yes, Redwood AE will handle onboarding and trial config, SE will run the benchmark and help with LangChain wiring, and CSM will be included if we move to Dedicated.
[09:43] Diego: quick note — our current client libs are in Node and Python, and we use LlamaIndex in a few services. We'll need both SDKs.
[09:50] Ravi: we have parity between Python and TypeScript SDKs; examples for LlamaIndex and LangChain will be included.
[09:58] Laura: any gotchas about streaming through kong?
[10:01] Priya: right now kong terminates connections for long lived streams unless configured. We'll need the NGINX/kong config you mentioned.
[10:09] Maya: I'll include advice: enable proxy_buffering off, set proper timeouts, and pass-through chunked transfer encoding.
[10:16] Wrap up / Recap:
- Redwood to send: LangChain & LlamaIndex adapter docs, Python/TS SDK snippets, kong/nginx streaming proxy configs, SOC2 + VPC checklist, Dedicated trial steps, and per-key rate limit header names.
- Argent action owners: share gateway diagram, list of headers to enforce, and prompt set for benchmark.

[10:40] Laura: thanks everyone, this was helpful. We'll review the examples and aim to start the trial next week.
[10:46] Maya: thanks, I'll email the materials and schedule the PoC scoping call for 3/19. Bye.

Notes on transcription: there are a few dropped words and speaker labels may be approximate. Some acronyms transcribed slightly off (KV cache as K V cash in one spot).
